proof_summary: Solving the continued-fraction recurrence gives it as \(X_2/X_3\), where \(X_2=(n+1)^2-5\), and a Casoratian identity involving \(X_3\) and \(2(n-1)!\) controls which factors cancel. Quadratic reciprocity supplies an even root \(m\) of \(5\bmod p\); with \(n=m-1\) and \(t=(m^2-5)/p\), parity, coprimality, and factorial divisibility show that reduction cancels exactly the cofactor \(t\) while leaving \(p\).
